ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Causal next-scale video prediction trained jointly with images
PROPOSAL: Extend a 2B next-scale image predictor to video by adding a causal temporal axis: clips are encoded into bitwise tokens at coarse-to-fine scales, and a scale is predicted in parallel given coarser scales and earlier frames. Train jointly on 5M captioned images and 2M captioned clips at 256p with seed 0. Evaluate text-to-video, image-to-video and extrapolation on VBench and a held-out set of 1000 prompts, and report latency per 5-second clip at 256p.
CONTROLS: Compare against a frame-by-frame variant of the same model, a variant with bidirectional temporal attention inside a scale, and a 2B diffusion baseline trained on identical data; ablate the joint mixture by training on clips only.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect the model to land within 3 VBench points of the diffusion baseline at about 5x lower latency; it could fail on fast motion, where coarse scales lose temporal detail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-backbone next-scale video model on a single clip corpus
PROPOSAL: Train an 8B transformer that predicts bitwise tokens scale by scale with causal attention over frames, drawing on the corpus of 3M captioned clips at 256p. Retrain the model from 5 initialisations to measure variance in VBench scores, then decode with the same checkpoints. Report text-to-video quality on a held-out set of 1000 prompts and latency per 5-second clip, with image-to-video results on 500 first frames.
CONTROLS: Compare against a frame-by-frame variant of the same backbone, a variant with bidirectional attention inside a scale, and a 2B diffusion baseline trained on the identical corpus; ablate the number of scales.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The 8B model should reach within 3 VBench points of the diffusion baseline at much lower latency; variance across initialisations should stay under 1 point, and long clips are the weak spot because early errors accumulate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Initialising a discrete video tokenizer from an image tokenizer
PROPOSAL: Build a causal video tokenizer by extending the 2D convolutions of a pretrained image tokenizer along time, with temporal compression of 4x. Train with reconstruction, perceptual and adversarial losses for 100000 updates at batch size 256 on 1M clips of 17 frames at 256p, using a codebook of 2^18 bitwise entries. Measure PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on 3000 held-out clips from the same source, and report the number of updates needed to reach an rFVD of 100.
CONTROLS: Compare against training the same tokenizer from scratch with identical losses, against the frozen image tokenizer applied frame by frame, and against a variant that freezes the extended weights early in training; use 2 seeds for the first comparison.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Initialising from the image tokenizer should reach the scratch tokenizer's rFVD in about a third of the updates; fine-tuning may fail to beat scratch training on clips with large camera motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tokenizer initialisation study across codebook sizes and corpora
PROPOSAL: Train causal video tokenizers with temporal compression of 4x on 3 corpora of 1M clips of 17 frames at 256p, initialised either from a pretrained image tokenizer or from random weights, with codebooks of 2^16, 2^18 and 2^20 bitwise entries. Use reconstruction, perceptual and adversarial losses. Measure PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on 3000 held-out clips from the matching corpus, and report the number of updates needed to reach an rFVD of 100 across seeds, with a long run of the 2^20 codebook to check convergence.
CONTROLS: Compare initialised against scratch tokenizers at all vocabulary sizes, against the frozen image tokenizer applied frame by frame, and against a variant that freezes the extended weights early in training; report spread over 6 seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Initialisation should reach the scratch rFVD in about a third of the updates at all vocabulary sizes; the advantage may shrink for the 2^20 codebook, where reconstruction detail depends less on the starting weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compressed history memory for long video continuation
PROPOSAL: Train a 2B causal next-scale model on 8-second clips and extend it to 40-second videos by letting new frames attend to full-resolution tokens from the last 2 seconds plus coarse-scale tokens of all earlier frames. Fine-tune on 300000 long videos at 360p, then generate 40-second continuations from 500 prompts and score subject consistency, background consistency and motion smoothness on VBench-Long, with latency recorded at 8, 24 and 40 seconds.
CONTROLS: Compare against full-history attention at 24 seconds, a sliding window with no coarse memory, and a version that drops the coarse tokens after 16 seconds; repeat these comparisons on 5 seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The compressed memory should keep consistency scores within 2 points of full-history attention while latency grows roughly linearly; drift in the subject's appearance beyond 30 seconds is where it could fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Window-limited history on a 12B backbone
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 12B causal next-scale model, pretrained on 8-second clips, on a corpus of 300000 long videos at 360p so that new frames attend to full-resolution tokens from the last 2 seconds. Restart the fine-tuning from 4 checkpoints taken at different pretraining stages, then generate 40-second continuations from 500 prompts and score subject consistency, background consistency and motion smoothness on VBench-Long, with latency at 8, 24 and 40 seconds.
CONTROLS: Compare against full-history attention at 24 seconds, a variant with a window of 4 seconds, and a variant with a window of 1 second; train all of them on 2 seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: A short window should keep consistency within 2 points of full history while latency grows roughly linearly; drift in the subject's appearance beyond 30 seconds is where it could fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progressive resolution training for 720p unified generation
PROPOSAL: Train a 3B discrete next-scale model through 3 resolution stages, 256p, 480p and 720p, on a mixture of 20M images and 4M captioned clips, adding scales as resolution rises and reusing the previous stage's weights. A single model handles text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video and extrapolation through task prefixes. Evaluate on VBench, GenEval and 1000 held-out prompts at 720p, reporting latency per 5-second clip against a 5B diffusion baseline.
CONTROLS: Compare progressive training with training at 720p from the start for a matched number of updates, a variant without task prefixes where separate heads are used, and a 5B diffusion baseline trained on the same data.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Progressive training should reach the quality of direct 720p training with far fewer updates; the unified model may lose some text-to-image fidelity relative to a specialist, visible on GenEval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct 720p training of a unified discrete video model
PROPOSAL: Train a 14B discrete next-scale model at 720p from the start on a mixture of 20M images and 4M captioned clips, restarting from 3 random initialisations to measure spread, then repeat the final stage on other data orderings. A single model handles text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video and extrapolation through task prefixes. Evaluate on VBench, GenEval and 1000 held-out prompts at 720p, reporting latency per 5-second clip against 5B and 14B diffusion baselines.
CONTROLS: Compare against a staged schedule with 3 resolutions, a variant without task prefixes where separate heads are used, and both diffusion baselines trained on the same data; report standard deviations over the 3 initialisations.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Direct training at 720p should match the staged schedule's quality, with spread across initialisations below 1 VBench point; text-to-image fidelity relative to a specialist is where it could fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bitwise versus index prediction for video tokens at small scale
PROPOSAL: Train two 600M causal next-scale models on 1M captioned clips at 128p: one predicts the bits of a 2^16 codebook entry with 16 binary heads, the other predicts the entry with a single softmax over 65536 classes. Measure token accuracy, rFVD of decoded samples on 2000 held-out clips and training stability through the gradient norm curve, then repeat the bitwise run with a codebook of 2^20 entries to see whether the gap between the two designs changes with vocabulary size.
CONTROLS: Compare against a factorised variant that splits the entry into 2 groups of 8 bits, and against a variant of the index model with label smoothing; use 2 seeds for both main models.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Bitwise prediction should match index prediction at 2^16 and pull ahead at 2^20, where the softmax becomes hard to train; at 2^12 the two should be indistinguishable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bitwise versus index prediction on a 7B video model
PROPOSAL: Train two 7B causal next-scale models on 1M captioned clips at 256p: one predicts the bits of a 2^16 codebook entry with 16 binary heads, the other predicts the entry with a single softmax over 65536 classes. Measure token accuracy, rFVD of decoded samples on 2000 held-out clips and training stability through the gradient norm curve, retraining both models from 4 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against a factorised variant splitting the entry into 2 groups of 8 bits, against an index model with label smoothing, and against a 600M pair trained on the same clips.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Bitwise prediction should match index prediction at this codebook size, with seed spread below 0.5 rFVD; instability of the single softmax is where the index model could fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-round video generation with keyframe history
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 3B discrete video model with a codebook of 2^16 on 150000 dialogues of 3 to 5 instruction turns at 256p, where the clip of a turn is conditioned on the new instruction, the last 2 seconds of the previous clip and 4 keyframes sampled from earlier turns. Build the dialogues by chaining captioned clips from one source with instructions written by a language model. Evaluate on 400 held-out dialogues with instruction-following scores from a video-language judge and subject consistency over turns.
CONTROLS: Compare against conditioning on the last clip only, against conditioning on the full token history, and against independent generation per turn; check judge scores against 200 human ratings.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Keyframe history should recover most of the consistency of full-history conditioning at a fraction of the sequence length; instructions that revert earlier edits are the likely failure, since keyframes may not encode them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-round video dialogues over several source corpora
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 3B discrete video model on 150000 dialogues of 3 to 5 instruction turns built by chaining captioned clips from 4 source corpora, with instructions written by language models. The clip of a turn is conditioned on the new instruction, the last 2 seconds of the previous clip and 4 keyframes from earlier turns. Evaluate on 400 held-out dialogues per corpus with instruction-following scores from 2 video-language judges and subject consistency over turns, repeating the fine-tuning on 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against conditioning on the last clip only, against conditioning on the full token history, and against independent generation per turn; check judge scores against 200 human ratings.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Keyframe history should recover most of the consistency of full-history conditioning at a fraction of the sequence length, with similar results across corpora; instructions that revert earlier edits are the likely failure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Positional schemes for video extrapolation beyond the training length
PROPOSAL: Train 1.5B causal next-scale models on 4-second clips at 24 frames per second with 3 temporal position schemes, rotary embeddings, learned absolute embeddings and relative bias, using 2M captioned clips at 256p. Generate continuations up to 16 seconds from 500 first clips and measure rFVD against ground-truth continuations from held-out videos, as well as frame-wise quality decay over time. Report the length at which quality falls below that of a freshly generated clip.
CONTROLS: Compare against a variant that rescales rotary frequencies at inference and a bidirectional diffusion model of 1.5B parameters that extends by sliding windows.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Rotary embeddings with rescaling should extrapolate to 4 times the training length with modest decay; learned absolute embeddings should break first, right after the training length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Position scheme comparison across clip lengths and seeds
PROPOSAL: Train 1.5B causal next-scale models with 3 temporal position schemes, rotary embeddings, learned absolute embeddings and relative bias, on 2M captioned clips at 256p, retraining from 6 seeds at training lengths of 2, 4 and 8 seconds. Generate continuations up to 16 seconds from 500 first clips and measure rFVD against ground-truth continuations from held-out videos, with frame-wise quality decay over time and the length at which quality falls below that of a fresh clip.
CONTROLS: Compare against a variant that rescales rotary frequencies at inference and a bidirectional diffusion model of 1.5B parameters that extends by sliding windows; report medians over 6 seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Rotary embeddings with rescaling should extrapolate to 4 times the training length with modest decay; learned absolute embeddings should break first, right after the training length, at all 3 training lengths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scale schedules trading latency against fidelity
PROPOSAL: Using a 2B next-scale video model on 256p clips, compare 4 schedules of scale resolutions with 6, 8, 10 and 13 scales, keeping the final token map fixed. Train all four on 3M captioned clips with identical updates, and measure VBench quality, rFVD on 2000 clips and generation latency per 5-second clip. Fit a curve of quality against number of forward passes and locate the knee of the curve.
CONTROLS: Compare against a diffusion baseline of 2B parameters with 20 and 50 sampling steps, and a schedule whose scales are spaced uniformly in token count rather than in resolution.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Quality should saturate near 10 scales, with the 6-scale schedule losing about 4 VBench points; at 13 scales latency rises with no visible gain, and the diffusion baseline stays slower at equal quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scale schedule study on a 9B model with a narrower schedule family
PROPOSAL: Using a 9B next-scale video model on 256p clips, train 3 schedules with 8, 10 and 13 scales, keeping the final token map fixed, on a corpus of 3M captioned clips with identical updates, and retrain all of them from 3 seeds. Measure VBench quality, rFVD on 2000 clips and generation latency per 5-second clip, then fit a curve of quality against forward passes.
CONTROLS: Compare against a diffusion baseline of 9B parameters with 20 and 50 sampling steps and a schedule spaced uniformly in token count.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Quality should saturate near 10 scales, with the 8-scale schedule losing about 2 VBench points; at 13 scales latency rises with no gain, and the diffusion baseline stays slower.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exposure bias across scales in a small next-scale video model
PROPOSAL: Train a 600M next-scale video model on 500000 captioned clips at 128p with teacher forcing, then measure how errors grow along the scale axis by feeding the model its own coarse predictions instead of true coarse tokens. Report token accuracy and rFVD on 1500 held-out clips as the number of self-generated scales rises from 0 to 8, and test a scheduled mix of true and generated coarse tokens at rates of 25% and 50%.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained with random token dropout in the coarse scales and against a model with a corrupted-context loss; 2 seeds for the main model.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Accuracy should fall sharply after the first 3 generated scales, and mixing in generated tokens during training should recover about half of the gap; the effect may vanish for clips with little motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Error propagation across scales under corrupted coarse tokens
PROPOSAL: Train a 6B next-scale video model with teacher forcing on 3 captioned corpora of 500000 clips at 256p, then replace true coarse tokens with tokens flipped at random rates of 5%, 10%, 20% and 40% before the finer scales are predicted. Report token accuracy and rFVD on 1500 held-out clips per corpus, and fit a decay curve of accuracy against the corruption rate over 5 seeds, followed by a rerun of the 20% setting with a flip pattern that follows motion boundaries.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained with random token dropout in the coarse scales and against a model with a corrupted-context loss; report spread over seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Accuracy should decay smoothly up to a 20% flip rate and then drop, with the motion-boundary pattern doing more damage at the same rate; the effect may vanish for static clips.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effect of video training on text-to-image quality
PROPOSAL: Start from a 3B text-to-image next-scale model trained on 30M images and continue training it as a unified model with video data at ratios of 0%, 10% and 30% clips, at 256p. Measure GenEval, FID on 30000 COCO prompts and VBench for text-to-video, and track forgetting by evaluating checkpoints every 5000 updates. Examine whether mixing in image batches during video training removes the loss in image quality.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original image model without further training, a model trained on clips only, and an image specialist continued on images alone for the same number of updates.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Video data at 10% should lower image quality by under 1 FID point, and 30% should lower it more but improve motion; a collapse of fine textures is the likely failure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image quality retention after video training of a 12B unified model
PROPOSAL: Start from a 12B text-to-image next-scale model trained on 30M images and continue it as a unified model with video data at a ratio of 20% clips, at 256p, retraining from 4 seeds. Measure GenEval, FID on 30000 COCO prompts and VBench for text-to-video, and track forgetting by evaluating checkpoints every 5000 updates.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original image model without further training, a model trained on clips only, and an image specialist continued on images alone for the same number of updates.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Video data at 20% should lower image quality by under 1 FID point, with seed spread below 0.3; a collapse of fine textures is the likely failure.
